questions.question: Explain the symmetry of flowers with suitable examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Explainthesymmetryofflowerswithsuitableexamples. /
  • Flower symmetry describes how the petals, sepals, and other floral parts can be divided into identical halves.
  • Three main types flowers are there based on their symmetry.
  • Actinomorphic (Radial Symmetry):
  • A flower that can be divided into two equal/identical halves along any vertical radial plane passing through the
  • center. e.g. Hibiscus, Allamanda, Ixora, etc
  • Zygomorphic (Bilateral Symmetry):
  • A flower that can be divided into two identical halves along only one single vertical plane passing through the
  • center. e.g. Clitoria, Crotalaria, Orchids, etc.
  • Asymmetric:
  • A flower that cannot be cut into two equal halves along any vertical plane through the center.
  • e.g. Canna indica.

questions.question: Comment on the importance of floras, revisions and monographs in plant taxonomy.
questions.solution_html:
• Commentontheimportanceoffloras,revisionsandmonographsinplanttaxonomy. /
  • Floras:
  • Books containing comprehensive descriptions, taxonomic keys, and distribution details of all plant species
  • inhabiting a specific geographical area (e.g., Flora of British India by J.D. Hooker, Flora of Presidency of
  • Madras by J.S. Gamble).
  • Importance of Floras: Essential field guide for rapid identification, local conservation strategies,
  • biodiversity assessment, and natural resource documentation.
  • Monographs:
  • Exhaustive, global taxonomic accounts of a single biological taxon (usually a genus or family) including
  • all species, synonomy, morphology, phylogeny, and geographical distribution worldwide.
  • Importance of monographs: Serves as the ultimate authority on worldwide variation within a specific
  • family/genus; solves taxonomic ambiguities.
  • Revisions:
  • Updated taxonomic re-examinations of previously published monographs or floristic treatments of specific
  • taxa within a region.
  • Importance of revisions: Incorporates new research findings (molecular, anatomical, palynological),
  • corrects nomenclature error, and updates classification in light of contemporary data.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: corrects nomenclature error, and updates classification in light of contemporary data.

questions.question: Identify the diagnostic features of Acanthaceae that are useful for family identification.
questions.solution_html:
• IdentifythediagnosticfeaturesofAcanthaceaethatareusefulforfamilyidentification . /
  • VegetativeCharacters:
  •  Herbaceous or shrubby habit with opposite decussate leaves.
  •  Stems frequently swollen at nodes; cystoliths (calcium carbonate deposits) present in epidermal cells.
  • FloralCharacters:
  •  Prominent, often brightly colored, overlapping bracts and bracteoles subtending flowers.
  •  Corolla: Bilabiate (2-lipped) or sub-equally 5-lobed, zygomorphic.
  •  Androecium: Usually 2 or 4 (didynamous) stamens inserted on the corolla tube.
  •  Gynoecium: Bicarpellary, syncarpous, superior ovary with axile placentation.
  •  Fruit is a loculicidal capsule.
  •  Seeds mounted on hook-like outgrowth of funicle called retinaculum (ejaculater) which helps in seed
  • dispersal.

questions.question: Write a short note on ICN.
questions.solution_html:
• WriteashortnoteonICN. /
  • ICN (International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants), formerly known as ICBN (renamed at the
  • Melbourne Congress in 2011). The International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants is the set of rules
  • and recommendations dealing with the formal botanical names that are given to plants, fungi and a few other groups
  • of organisms, all those "traditionally treated as algae, fungi, or plants".
  • Key Principles:
  •  Botanical nomenclature is independent of zoological and bacteriological nomenclature.
  •  Type Concept (Nomenclatural Types): Application of names of taxonomic groups is determined by means of
  • nomenclatural types (holotype, isotype, lectotype, neotype).
  •  Principle of Priority: The correct name of a taxon is the earliest validly published name in accordance with the
  • rules
  •  Unique Name Rule: Each taxonomic group with a particular circumscription, position, and rank can bear only
  • one correct name.
  •  Scientific names are treated as Latin regardless of derivation.
  •  Rules of nomenclature are retroactive unless expressly limited.
  • (AnyfivevalidpointsaboutICNcanbeconsideredforfullmarks )

questions.question: Analyse the advanced features of the family Asteraceae that make it one of the most successful angiosperm families.
questions.solution_html:
• AnalysetheadvancedfeaturesofthefamilyAsteraceaethatmakeitoneofthemostsuccessful
  • angiospermfamilies.
  • /
  •  Inflorescence Aggregation (Capitulum/Head) : Hundreds of small flowers (florets) gathered together into a
  • single head mimicking one large flower, maximizing pollinator visibility with minimal tissue expenditure.
  •  Specialized Pollination Mechanism : Piston/plunger (syngenesious) pollination mechanism ensuring
  • efficient cross-pollination and backup self-pollination.
  •  Modification of Calyx into Pappus : Calyx modified into hairy, feathery, or awned structures (pappus)
  • aiding in widespread anemochorous (wind) seed dispersal.
  •  The syngenesious condition —where anthers are fused laterally to form a hollow tube while filaments
  • remain free—plays a crucial role in the evolutionary and reproductive success of the Asteraceae family
  •  Epigynous Flower & Single Seed Protection : Inferior bicarpellary ovary yielding a single-seeded cypsela
  • fruit, directing energy into a single viable offspring per floret.
  •  Chemical Defense Mechanisms : Rich production of secondary metabolites discouraging herbivores and
  • pathogens.
  •  Ecological Adaptability: Herbaceous habit with short life cycles enabling rapid colonization across diverse
  • biomes.
  • ( Any five valid points can be considered for full marks )
